The problem: QtCreator and GTK Glade Editor in general suck, are buggy, restrictive to it's respective language choice, lack a friendly way to customize themes and be unintuitive to new developers and experienced developers alike and we need a better solution than this for Native GUI application development.

Solution?

HTML/CSS Compiler

HTML/CSS Compiler which compile HTML/CSS into C as native GUI.

I think using HTML/CSS would offer the best choice to developers for GUI development, because it is perhaps the most intutive scripting language for designing a page for an application, but instead of requiring a web browser or slapping embedded web browser on the window, we compile the HTML/CSS into the application window itself steamlining the process in C or whichever languages. I would prefer that it represent from X11 directly as to remove dependencies, but it can represent from QT, GTK, WxForm, SDL or any GUI frameworks if anyone really want to go that far.

Having something like this make it hell a lot easier to divide the tasks between designers and developers. This enables people to make a more fancier applications ranging in all kinds of styles and designs that are familiar to people.

As for how HTML/CSS can be compiled and represented in C, I'll explain. HTML/CSS can be compiled into a library that depends on the base library which contains all the controls, instructions, and event handling codes for all what compiled C HTML/CSS codes needed. This simplify how different languages can bind to the same base library and be used equally across any languages that developer wish to use. When people want to include a new compiled HTML/CSS page to their application, they simply load it by either dynamic loading from the base library framework, invoke the code directly with HTML/CSS compiled in C source code/header files, or run it as a standalone.

Reason why I suggested C as the primary language is that it is much more easier to bind C code to different languages than C++ or any other languages and that isn't a debate. Also javascript support could be optional to those who want to support it, but I would imagine that it would introduce a lot of unneeded headaches.

Thought? Criticisms? Did I miss any?

Thank you for reading.
